The main process keeps the app responsive: menus, the tray, creating windows and native dialogs all run there. The sync engine's work would block it. `node:sqlite` is synchronous, so a catch-up batch writing thousands of rows freezes whichever thread runs it, and in main that shows up as the whole app stalling. Full-text search queries over a large corpus have no real upper limit on how long they take, either (`docs/DESIGN.md:306-315`).

Running it separately also means a crash doesn't take the app down. If the engine hangs or throws on a malformed frame, main restarts it after a second and the user's windows stay open (`apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts:122-126`). Putting it in a utility process rather than a renderer matters too. The WebSocket survives window reloads and closes, it isn't subject to Chromium's background timer throttling (a spike measured that), and there's a single socket and database writer no matter how many windows are open. Renderers talk to it directly over a `MessagePort`, so main isn't relaying messages on the busiest path (`docs/DESIGN.md:321-330`, `2575-2596`).
